statement: A set $S$ of positive reals is \textit{Aristotelian} if for any $x < y < z$ in $S$, $\dfrac{z-x}{y} \in S$. Find all integers $n \geq 4$ for which there exists an Aristotelian set with exactly $n$ elements.

A $2n \times 2n$ board is tiled with $2 \times 1$ and $1 \times 2$ dominoes. To \textit{pivot} a domino: choose one of its unit squares and rotate the entire domino by $90^\circ$, $-90^\circ$, or $180^\circ$ about that square's center. Prove it is always possible to simultaneously pivot every domino so that the dominoes still tile the board.

Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle DAB < 90^\circ$ and $AB < AD$. Let $H$ be the orthocenter of $\triangle BCD$ and $H'$ the reflection of $H$ over $BD$. Line $AH$ meets $BD$, $CD$, $BC$ at $E$, $F$, $G$. Prove the circumcircles of $\triangle HEH'$ and $\triangle CFG$ are tangent.

Let $n \geq 2$. The number $1$ is written $n$ times. An operation: choose two numbers $a, b$ (not both zero) and replace them with $\dfrac{(a-b)^2}{a+b}$ and $\dfrac{4ab}{a+b}$. Find all $n$ for which it is possible, after finitely many operations, for $n$ to appear on the blackboard.
